This exceeds typical May climatological highs of 23–24°C due to persistent dry air advection over the past week. Realistic challenges include a late-afternoon convective burst boosting surface heating or a station-specific measurement revision, though model uncertainty is minimal as the resolution window nears evening.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket clusters around 22–25°C for Paris's highest temperature on May 9, reflecting the latest ECMWF and GFS ensemble forecasts showing means near 23°C amid a transitional spring pattern with mild southerly flow. Recent model runs over the past 48 hours indicate slight warming from earlier weekly outlooks of 19°C, driven by a potential high-pressure ridge weakening Atlantic cloud bands, though persistent shower risks and variable cloud cover create the tight spread between outcomes—sunny breaks could push toward 25°C, while overcast skies favor 22°C. Above the May 9 historical average of 19°C, uncertainty stems from frontal timing; monitor Météo-France updates and ECMWF refreshes on May 8 for shifts ahead of resolution at Paris-Le Bourget Airport.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest INMET forecasts project a maximum temperature of 28°C for São Paulo on May 9 under mostly cloudy conditions with light northerly winds and low humidity, driving trader consensus toward 29°C (25.5% implied probability), 28°C (23.5%), and 27°C (21.0%) amid tight clustering. Southeast Brazil's persistent high-pressure ridge has sustained above-average early-May warmth (historical highs ~23–24°C), with dry stability over the past week limiting cooling. New INMET advisories and model updates expected by May 8 could sharpen resolution odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's latest 5-day outlook for Port Area in Metro Manila forecasts a 34-35°C high on May 9 amid partly cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms from easterlies, driving trader consensus to tightly cluster implied probabilities around 34-37°C at 25-27% each. Recent observations underscore this uncertainty: Science Garden in Quezon City hit 35.5°C and NAIA Pasay reached 36.3°C on May 6 during the ongoing dry-season heatwave, where urban heat island effects amplify actual air temperatures beyond averages of 33-34°C for May. Differentiating factors include potential sea breeze moderation versus prolonged sunshine boosting peaks to 37°C, with daily PAGASA updates and new model runs expected to refine guidance ahead of resolution based on the official station reading.
